clue.text: Swift and quiet in attack

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for quiet sits inside the word for attack

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
P (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A military assault that is both fast and silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe great speed of movement; they are synonyms.

clue.text: A fine state to be in

definitions.text: A fine state to be in

parts.words: A fine state to be in
parts.note: the idiom 'in fine ...' describes being in good health or condition, so the clue points to the noun for condition

explanation.walkthrough: 'A fine state' sounds ironic (a mess), but the clue is a straight hint at the stock phrase 'in fine fettle'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means condition or shape, heard mostly in the stock phrase for good health.

clue.text: Tees should be made with sand — agreed?

indicators.note: the letters should be made into something new, so the two words are rearranged together

explanation.surface: A question about whether golf tees ought to be made from sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be made' asks for TEES and SAND to be rearranged together; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To consent to something is to say yes to it, a synonym of the past tense here.

clue.text: It's the driver's right in Britain

definitions.text: It's the driver's right in Britain

parts.words: It's the driver's right in Britain
parts.note: read as a statement about entitlement it is about rights; really it names which side of a car the driver sits on in a country that drives on the left

explanation.walkthrough: British cars drive on the left with the driver on the right, and that right-hand side is called by a word that also names a football rule.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the side of a vehicle nearest the middle of the road, the driver's side, has this name.

clue.text: Dispatched about ten cents as a deposit

indicators.note: about here means going around, so the word for dispatched surrounds the coin

parts.note: dispatched means sent off
a dime is the US coin worth ten cents

explanation.surface: Someone posted a dime to put down as a deposit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is matter that settles and is laid down, in geology a deposit.

clue.text: First on the list of Christmas presents

definitions.text: First on the list of Christmas presents

parts.words: First on the list of Christmas presents
parts.note: points to the carol 'The Twelve Days of Christmas', whose first gift is a bird in a pear tree

explanation.walkthrough: The 'list' is not a child's wish list but the carol 'The Twelve Days of Christmas', where the first day's gift is the bird in a pear tree.
explanation.definitionFit: In the carol the true love's first-day gift is this game bird.

clue.text: Past offer may result in contracts

indicators.note: the letters may result in something else when rearranged, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: An offer made earlier might lead to signed business agreements.
explanation.definitionFit: Contracts as a verb means narrows or dwindles, the sense of gradually reducing.

clue.text: It could be a four-legged race

definitions.text: It could be a four-legged race

parts.words: It could be a four-legged race
parts.note: suggests an animal race, but means a race run in four legs or stages by a team

explanation.walkthrough: 'four-legged' suggests horses; it means four stages, each run by a different team member.
explanation.definitionFit: A team race in which each runner covers one stage, typically four of them.

clue.text: Love to drink up after work

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for drink is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: An invitation to drink up after the working day is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SUP into PUS, placed after O; 'after work' looks like time, but 'work' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary composition, a creative work.

clue.text: Stride about on the ship when there's trouble

indicators.note: on places the ship after the rearranged letters in an across answer
about signals that the letters of stride are moved around

parts.note: SS is the standard abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone paces up and down the deck when things go wrong at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges STRIDE to DISTRE, then SS follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is suffering or difficulty, a synonym for trouble.

clue.text: It's normally found at the foot of the column

definitions.text: It's normally found at the foot of the column

parts.words: It's normally found at the foot of the column
parts.note: suggests the bottom of a newspaper column, but means the base block beneath a pillar

explanation.walkthrough: 'column' sounds like print journalism, but it is an architectural pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A plinth is the square slab or block on which a pillar or statue stands.

clue.text: Tendency to be dishonest

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an inclination or knack and, in slang, crooked or corrupt.

clue.text: Six delay treating word-blindness

indicators.note: treating means processing the letters, working them into a new order

explanation.surface: Six patients wait too long before being treated for a reading disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Word-blindness is an older term for the learning difficulty affecting reading.

clue.text: Snaps come out and go round

indicators.note: out means the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Photographs emerge and are passed around.
explanation.definitionFit: To encompass is to surround or encircle, to go all the way around.

clue.text: He's not a particular person

parts.note: reads as someone who isn't fussy, but means any person at all, no specific one

explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun refers to any person whatever rather than a specific individual.

clue.text: A rest for anyone who's still alive

definitions.meaning: one who still draws breath, read literally

explanation.surface: Only the living get to take a break.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pause is this, and so, literally, is anyone who still breathes.

clue.text: One who enjoys being patronised

parts.note: patronised usually means talked down to, but here it means supported by a patron

explanation.walkthrough: Nobody enjoys condescension; 'patronised' here means sponsored by a patron.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a person guided and supported by an influential mentor or sponsor.

clue.text: A Cortina's changing gear in wet weather

indicators.note: changing signals the letters are being altered into a new order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter; the word is taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone changing gear in a Ford Cortina while it rains.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cortina was a popular British Ford car; 'changing gear' sounds like driving, but 'gear' means clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof coat is clothing worn when it rains.

clue.text: Be a toff disguised, being eccentric

indicators.note: disguised means the letters are dressed up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A posh person in disguise behaving oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unconventional or odd is described this way, a synonym of eccentric.

clue.text: It won't be found in the pack

definitions.text: It won't be found in the pack

parts.words: It won't be found in the pack
parts.note: a pack could be cards, but here it is a group of wild hunting animals

explanation.walkthrough: 'pack' tempts towards cards; it is a pack of wolves, and the loner stays outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary person who prefers acting alone, from the animal living apart from its pack.

clue.text: Ring New York before ten? It will be expensive

indicators.note: before places New York ahead of the ten in the down answer

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A ring bought in New York before ten o'clock will cost a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a semi-precious banded stone, so a piece of it costs money.

clue.text: Knight I sent back for the flag

indicators.note: sent back means the knight's title and I are read in reverse order

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: A knight returns the banner he was given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses SIR + I; 'flag' is not a banner but the plant also called the yellow flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is an old name for wild plants of this genus, such as the yellow water variety.

clue.text: Introduce gradually in new list

indicators.note: new means the letters of list are made fresh in another order

explanation.surface: Advice to bring something in bit by bit within a fresh list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges LIST to STIL, after IN taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil is to implant an idea or habit slowly over time.

clue.text: She turns the tide at Holyhead

indicators.note: turns means the letters of tide are turned about into a new order

parts.note: the head of the word Holy, its first letter, H

explanation.surface: A woman who reverses the tide at the Welsh port of Holyhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Holyhead is a Welsh ferry port; read as 'Holy head' it gives H. 'turns' rearranges TIDE to EDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith is a woman's name, so it can stand for the pronoun.

clue.text: One is not keen to show it

definitions.text: One is not keen to show it

parts.words: One is not keen to show it
parts.note: describes the state someone displays when they lack any enthusiasm

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like reluctance to reveal something, but it describes what an unenthusiastic person displays.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is lack of interest or enthusiasm, what an indifferent person displays.

clue.text: Bottom team after defender

indicators.note: after puts the team after the defender in an across answer

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football or rugby
a side is a team

explanation.surface: The bottom team in the league comes in after the defender.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottom in its anatomical sense, the buttocks, is a synonym.

clue.text: She appears in an ensemble that's rather colourless

indicators.note: appears in tells us the pronoun shows up inside the little word an

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman takes part in a group performance that lacks colour.
explanation.walkthrough: SHE goes inside AN; 'ensemble' only supports the surface of a stage group.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means pale or grey-faced, drained of colour.

clue.text: New assistant for the devil-worshippers

indicators.note: new signals the letters are formed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A new helper for the cult that worships the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who worship Satan, the devil, take their name from him.
